question_suffix: Respond using exactly these three lines: Recommendation: <one sentence> Reason: <one sentence> Caveat: <one sentence>. Keep the whole answer between 45 and 60 words. Use plain language. Do not mention the instruction, moral theory names, or any of these words: duty, duties, right, rights, promise, promises, obligation, obligations, constraint, constraints, commitment, commitments, boundary, boundaries, forbidden.

conditions.description: Controlled primary deontological stance with duties, rights, promises, and obligations.
conditions.instruction: Answer as someone who gives priority to duties, rights, promises, and obligations even when another option seems beneficial.

conditions.description: Controlled deontological variant with commitments, firm boundaries, and lines that should not be crossed.
conditions.instruction: Answer as someone who gives priority to commitments, firm boundaries, and lines that should not be crossed even when another option seems beneficial.

conditions.description: Controlled generic moral anchor with the same output regime but no deontological framing.
conditions.instruction: Answer as someone trying to make a morally careful recommendation even when the situation is difficult.

conditions.description: Controlled neutral anchor with the same output regime and no moral-framework wording.
conditions.instruction: Read the situation carefully and give a careful recommendation even when the situation is difficult.

conditions.description: Controlled anti-deont diagnostic with both lexical families suppressed as decisive reasons.
conditions.instruction: Answer without treating duties, rights, promises, obligations, commitments, or boundaries as decisive.
